solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Robert’s court cases start on Monday, police dealing with mine? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.cases: Robert's 'cases' (encloses) the M, as a box holds its contents

blocks.note: Bob is short for Robert, so Robert's = BOB'S
first letter of Monday, placed inside BOBS to make BOMBS
a quad (quadrangle) is a college court

annotation.surface: A man called Robert has a run of court hearings beginning on Monday.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a legal diary, but the court is a college quadrangle. The question mark flags that 'mine' is an explosive mine, not the possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A bomb squad is the police unit that deals with explosive devices such as mines.

entries.clue: Charging point on route? (3,4)

blocks.note: the surface pushes an electric-car charger; the setter means a place where passengers pile on, or are charged their fares
the route is a bus route, with its fixed stopping places

annotation.surface: Reads like a place on a journey where an electric car gets its battery topped up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charging point' suggests electric vehicles; here it is where a bus takes on passengers, or charges them their fares, on its route.
annotation.definitionFit: A bus stop is the point on a bus route where passengers board and pay.

entries.clue: Join M11 northbound after mile (3)

indicatorNotes.northbound: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so XI turns round
indicatorNotes.after: IX is placed after the M for mile

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for mile
the M of the motorway name, surface only once mile has supplied the M
11 in Roman numerals is XI, turned round to IX

annotation.surface: An instruction to get onto the M11 motorway heading north.
annotation.walkthrough: The M11 is a motorway north out of London. Its M does double duty: read it as mile, and the XI after it must turn round to head north.
annotation.definitionFit: To mix is to join or combine things together.

entries.clue: Large maned male on which sat jockeys? (8)

annotation.definition: Large maned male on which sat jockeys?

indicatorNotes.jockeys: to jockey is to jostle about, so the letters of SAT are shuffled
indicatorNotes.on which: in a down clue, STA sits on top of L + LION

blocks.note: SAT with its letters rearranged
L = large, as on clothing labels
the male lion has the mane

annotation.surface: A big male horse with a mane, ridden by jockeys.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a stallion is a large maned male that jockeys sit on. 'On which' works because in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, maned and large, which jockeys ride.

entries.clue: Unqualified and articulate (5)

blocks.note: adjective: without qualification, complete, total
verb: to put into words, to say

annotation.walkthrough: Unqualified as in 'utter nonsense', complete; articulate as a verb, to speak.
annotation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute or unqualified, and also to say or articulate something.

entries.clue: Joyce’s work is to name ships (9)

blocks.note: to dub is to give a name to
liners are large passenger ships

annotation.surface: Someone claims James Joyce's job is christening ships.
annotation.walkthrough: Dubliners is James Joyce's 1914 short-story collection; 'work' means a literary work, not a job.
annotation.definitionFit: Dubliners is a book of short stories by James Joyce.

entries.clue: Passage of play understood from commentary (5)

indicatorNotes.from commentary: a commentary is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: seen = understood, as in 'I see'

annotation.surface: A stretch of a match that became clear from listening to the commentary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passage of play' sounds like sport; here the play is a drama, and a scene is one passage of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plays are divided into acts and those into scenes, so each one is a passage of the drama.

entries.clue: Quiet type’s removing top, part of strip (6)

indicatorNotes.removing top: the first letter, the top of a down entry, is taken away

blocks.note: sh! = be quiet
type = SORT, so type's = SORTS; removing its top S leaves ORTS

annotation.surface: A reserved person slips off their top, as in a striptease.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests undressing; the strip is a sports team's kit, of which shorts are part.
annotation.definitionFit: Shorts are part of a footballer's strip, the kit a team wears.

entries.clue: Engineer dated Anthony informally — ring declined, by the sound of it? (7,4)

annotation.definition: ring declined, by the sound of it?

blocks.note: Eng. is the abbreviation for engineer
dated = old, aged
Tone is a pet form of Tony, itself short for Anthony

annotation.surface: An engineer went out with Anthony, but he turned down her ring.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a rejected proposal; the definition means a phone call that doesn't connect, which you know from the sound on the line.
annotation.definitionFit: An engaged tone is the sound heard when a phone call cannot be put through because the line is busy.

entries.clue: Singer seized by signs of hesitation making mistake (7)

indicatorNotes.seized by: what is seized is gripped on both sides, so RAT sits held between ER and UM

blocks.note: er, the first sign of hesitation
a rat is an informer, one who sings to the police
um, the second sign of hesitation

annotation.surface: A nervous singer, all ers and ums, fluffs a line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is not a vocalist but an informer: someone who sings to the police is a rat.
annotation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error, especially one in print.

entries.clue: Term for species surviving sixty degrees (7)

indicatorNotes.Term for: a term is an end, so the term of species is its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of species
an extant species is one still surviving

annotation.surface: A biological label for a species that has not died out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Term for species' looks like taxonomy; 'term' here means end. A sextant is a sixth of a circle, which is sixty degrees.
annotation.definitionFit: A sextant is one sixth of a circle, an arc of sixty degrees, which gives the instrument its name.

entries.clue: British chopper down in the forest, correspondent on site (7)

blocks.note: B = British
a logger fells trees

annotation.surface: A British helicopter crashed in the woods, and a reporter is on the scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopper down' reads as a crashed helicopter; it is a person chopping trees down. The site is a website.
annotation.definitionFit: A blogger writes for a website, a correspondent whose pieces appear on a site.

entries.clue: Skin drier until nearly healthy (5)

indicatorNotes.nearly: not quite all of WELL: the last letter goes

blocks.note: as in 'nine to five'
healthy = WELL, nearly = without its last L

annotation.surface: Skin stays drier until it is nearly well again, like healing eczema.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drier' reads as the comparative of dry; it is the noun, a thing that dries your skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A towel is what you dry your skin with.

entries.clue: If some law’s broken crossing road, no comment is possible (5,4,2)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters of IF SOME LAW are broken up and rearranged
indicatorNotes.crossing: the rearranged letters lie across RD, holding it inside

blocks.note: IF SOME LAW rearranged, split round RD
Rd is the abbreviation for road

annotation.surface: When a rule gets broken at a road crossing, the speaker is lost for words.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of law's reads as 'is': the law is broken. RD sits inside the anagram, W O (RD) S F A I L M E.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Words fail me' is what you say when you are too shocked to comment.

entries.clue: Proper coats are not unusually weatherproof (9)

indicatorNotes.coats: RIGHT is wrapped round AINT, as a coat covers what is inside

blocks.note: proper = right, correct; it takes AINT after its first letter
ain't is a non-standard way of saying are not

annotation.surface: Good coats are, surprisingly, not waterproof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' looks like an anagram indicator; it marks ain't as an unusual, non-standard form of are not. Result R(AINT)IGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Raintight means keeping rain out, weatherproof.

entries.clue: Somebody distributed oranges following sport at school (9)

indicatorNotes.distributed: the letters of ORANGES are dealt out in a new order

blocks.note: PE = physical education, school sport
ORANGES rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone handed out oranges after the school games lesson, as at half-time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somebody' is the definition as a noun: a somebody, an important person.
annotation.definitionFit: Both mean a person of some importance: to be a somebody is to be a figure of note.

entries.clue: Snatch crust of bread during sale (9)

indicatorNotes.crust of: a crust is the outside, so the outer letters of bread
indicatorNotes.during: what happens during something falls within its span, so BD goes inside AUCTION

blocks.note: an auction is a sale; BD goes in after its A
outer letters of bread

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a bread crust at a sale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snatch' is a noun here, a kidnapping. A(BD)UCTION.
annotation.definitionFit: Snatch is informal for a kidnapping, the seizing of a person, which is the formal word's meaning too.

entries.clue: Paradisal cove with a bar across the stream (4)

blocks.note: as written
a barrier built to hold back a river's water

annotation.surface: A heavenly bay with a sandbar across a stream flowing into it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cove' reads as a bay; it is old slang for a man. The man in Paradise, the Garden of Eden, is Adam.
annotation.definitionFit: Adam was the man, the cove, living in the paradise of Eden.

entries.clue: Fellow tenant under no pressure, finishing check (8)

blocks.note: a tyre with no pressure is flat
checkmate is the check that finishes a chess game

annotation.surface: A relaxed tenant finishing a check of the property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finishing check' is the chess checkmate, mate for short.
annotation.definitionFit: A flatmate is someone you share a rented flat with, a fellow tenant.

entries.clue: Shed about a stone (4)

blocks.note: ca. = circa, about
st = stone, the weight

annotation.surface: A garden shed weighing roughly fourteen pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shed' is the verb, as a snake sheds or casts its skin. A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: To cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin.

entries.clue: Qualified about a year, sad leaving university (7)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the U for university leaves BLUE

blocks.note: ca. = circa, about
p.a. = per annum, a year
sad = BLUE, minus its U
U, the letter that leaves BLUE

annotation.surface: A student qualified after about a year and left university unhappy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A year' is the two letters PA, per annum, not A + Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Capable and qualified both mean competent to do something.

entries.clue: Inconsistent Liberal accustomed to the left and right wing (9)

indicatorNotes.to the left: USED is written leftwards, giving DESU

blocks.note: used (to) = accustomed, written backwards
L = Liberal
the Tories are the British right-wing party

annotation.surface: A politician who flits between left and right is called inconsistent.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is political, but 'the left' is a direction for writing USED backwards. Tory means a member of the British Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Desultory means erratic, lacking consistency or purpose.

entries.clue: Vote for split when profits are calculated (4-3)

blocks.note: yea is a vote in favour
to rend is to tear apart

annotation.surface: Shareholders vote for a split when the accounts are done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a share split or a division of profits; it is the verb rend.
annotation.definitionFit: The year-end is when a company closes its books and works out its profits.

entries.clue: Tough precinct in need of Detective Inspector (6)

indicatorNotes.in need of: to be in need of something is to lack it, so the word goes without DI

blocks.note: a precinct is an area of a city under one police station; lose DI from the front
DI, the letters removed

annotation.surface: A rough police district needs a detective inspector.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a TV cop show; 'in need of' means without, so DISTRICT loses DI.
annotation.definitionFit: Strict means tough, firm about rules.

entries.clue: Adhesive covering back of map apparently synthetic (9)

indicatorNotes.covering back of: STICKY is laid over the end of PLAN, hiding its N

blocks.note: map = PLAN, with its back letter N covered
adhesive = sticky

annotation.surface: Sticky tape over the back of a map looks like plastic.
annotation.walkthrough: STICKY does not wrap round anything: it covers the last letter of PLAN, so the N disappears from view.
annotation.definitionFit: Plasticky means looking or feeling like plastic, apparently synthetic.

entries.clue: Fast boat yards ahead of German eight (5)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: in a down entry, what is ahead comes first, so Y leads and ACHT follows

blocks.note: y = yards
acht is German for eight

annotation.surface: A quick vessel just yards ahead of a German rowing eight.
annotation.walkthrough: An 'eight' in rowing is a crew boat, which makes the race picture; here it is just the number in German.
annotation.definitionFit: A yacht is a light, fast sailing or racing boat.

entries.clue: Mark Zoë has from wetsuit remains (5)

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken from inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of wetsuit into the start of remains

annotation.surface: Zoë's wetsuit still bears a mark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a stain on the wetsuit; it is the two dots over the ë in Zoë.
annotation.definitionFit: A trema is the diaeresis, the two-dot mark over the e in Zoë.

entries.clue: Noise at end of lesson contained by one Italian master (7)

indicatorNotes.contained by: N is held between the two Is

blocks.note: a bell makes a noise
I = one, the Roman numeral
last letter of lesson
I = Italian

annotation.surface: The bell ringing at the end of a lesson taught by an Italian maestro.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian master' looks like the definition, but Italian gives an I. Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian Renaissance painter, an old master.
annotation.definitionFit: Bellini was one of the great Venetian painters, an old master.

entries.clue: Silly to turn to carbon — be sustainable (7)

annotation.definitionNote: Silly is used as a noun here, a silly person, matching the noun charlie

blocks.note: to char is to burn to carbon
in law, an action that lies is one that can be sustained

annotation.surface: It is foolish to burn things to carbon when you should live sustainably.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sustainable' reads as green; LIE comes from the legal sense, where a claim 'lies' if it can be sustained. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a fool, a silly.

entries.clue: Pin is what keeps your hair in place when up (3)

indicatorNotes.when up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so GEL turns round

blocks.clueFragment: what keeps your hair in place
blocks.note: hair gel holds a style in place

annotation.surface: A hairpin is what holds your hair when it is worn up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pin' suggests a hairpin; it is slang for a leg, as in 'wobbly on my pins'.
annotation.definitionFit: Pins is informal British for legs, so a pin is a leg.

entries.clue: Still time for something to happen (5)

blocks.note: still = even, as in 'even better'
T = time

annotation.surface: There is still time for something to occur.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still time' reads as a phrase; split it, still = EVEN and time = T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything that happens, or is scheduled to happen, is an event.

entries.clue: Fan urged on team, ultimately beaten at football (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of team

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan
last letter of team
egged on = urged on

annotation.surface: A supporter cheered the side on, but they lost the match in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: To nutmeg a player is to kick the ball through their legs and run past them, so they are beaten.
annotation.definitionFit: Nutmegged means beaten by having the ball played between your legs in football.
